subject: chemistry
question_text: Calculate the kinetic energy of 2 moles of nitrogen at 27 °C.

verification.note: Chapter 4 (States of Matter) is sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack chemistry section (book pp.62-66), which prints the question, its star rank and a model answer. Only ONE source book is held for chemistry — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only — so the two-book union check is PENDING a second chemistry source. The book prints NO Long Answer section for this chapter, so no 8-mark form is invented. The 1+1 mark split is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it; the question itself is sourced, not invented. ARITHMETIC: the book answers 1800 calories using R = 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (a rounding of 1.987). This card works in SI (7.48 × 10³ J) and shows the calorie form beside it; the two agree within the rounding of R. This question repeats the book's three-star VSAQ 5 with n = 2 instead of n = 5 — both are asked, so both are authored. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25. Arithmetic re-verified: 1.5 × 2 × 8.314 × 300 = 7482.6 J ≈ 7.48 × 10³ J, and the calorie form 1.5 × 2 × 2 × 300 = 1800 cal — both printed values correct. Added one clause to the first step's why saying (3/2)nRT is the TRANSLATIONAL kinetic energy, so a student who knows N₂ is diatomic is not told the card is wrong. No marked line changed. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25 (audit round): the calorie line called 1800 cal the same energy in calories, but 7482.6 J is 1788 cal; the two figures agree only under the rounded R = 2, so the bracket now says that instead of claiming an exact equality.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Formula and substitution
steps.why: KE = (3/2)nRT holds for any gas — the identity of nitrogen never enters. (This is the translational kinetic energy the kinetic gas equation gives; a molecule is treated as a moving point, so the same (3/2)nRT is used for diatomic N₂.) The only work before substitution is converting 27 °C to 300 K.
common_mistakes: Bringing the molar mass of N₂ into the formula. Kinetic energy of n moles needs no molar mass.
steps.memory_tip: Three halves n R T — the gas's name is a distraction; only n and T matter.
steps.margin_note: The formula with T = 300 K earns this mark before any arithmetic.

steps.label: The answer with its unit
lines: With R ≈ 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹: KE = (3/2) × 2 × 2 × 300
= 1800 cal (using the rounded R = 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
steps.why: 2 × 8.314 = 16.628; times 300 gives 4988.4; times 1.5 gives 7482.6 J. The calorie line reproduces the book's expected 1800 cal with the rounded R = 2 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹.
common_mistakes: Writing the number with no unit.
Mixing R values — 8.314 gives joules, 2 gives calories; using one and naming the other's unit.
steps.memory_tip: Two moles at room temperature: about twice 3.7 kJ, near 7.5 kJ.
steps.margin_note: Box the SI value; the calorie line is the book's form of the same answer.

insider_note: This is the n = 5 question again with n = 2 — the paper-setters reuse the template, so master the template once and read n carefully on the day.
